title: Signoff v2 input
description: The one validated input structure of the portable signoff core (signoff-contract.md section 2). A calling station passes it whole; direct invocation builds it from the user's request and the workspace. Checks a schema cannot express - run_dir outside the workspace, build_doc containment after symbolic links, a base that does not resolve - belong to the path rules and the source-set computation, which report them as stops rather than as schema errors. Every object is closed, so an unknown key is refused rather than ignored.

protocol_version.description: the version of this shape; a new required field or a changed meaning is a new version

run_id.description: one path segment, fresh for a new run; the run directory's receipt settles a run that was killed

run_dir.description: absolute scratch path OUTSIDE the workspace; every artifact of the run lands here

run_date.description: the date the block heading carries and every event of the run carries in its `at`; today in UTC when absent

harness.description: the harness the run is executing in, recorded on every event's actor

building.description: the session that built the slice; null when it is not known

reviewing.description: the session doing the reviewing. Equal to `building` is the independence refusal, not a warning

model.description: the reviewing session's model and whether it meets the Opus-class floor. A floor this run cannot establish is a stop, never an assumption (v1 Step 0)

workspace.description: absolute path of the git work tree root under review

build_doc.description: the ledger document, workspace-relative: never one under docs/records/ (the component's history) or docs/reviews/ (a mirror), which the component refuses with exit 4

slice.description: the slice inside that document, as its `## Slice <X>` heading names it

base.description: the git ref naming the slice's base. A ref that does not resolve is a stop, never a guess

report_only.description: when true the run writes nothing to the workspace and nothing to the log, and its result says so

depth.description: v1 Step 3's depths. LEAN is three lenses; DEEP adds security and tests; LIGHT is one fused reviewer and is never self-selected

lenses.description: the lenses this run sends; the depth's own set when absent

route.description: how the reviewer is reached, recorded with what it concluded (E13-4). `readers:<row>` in a live run

builder_conversation.description: workspace-relative paths the caller declares to be the builder's own account of its work. They stay IN the source set and IN the packet's file list; their CONTENT is withheld from the delivered material (amendment A3 item 2)
